name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, metallising, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: A quiet week: no company filing, ECMS tranche or duty notification on capacitor film. The new data point is QYResearch's sizing of the global capacitor-grade BOPP market (USD 874.5 mn in 2025, 6.25% CAGR to 2032). It names Xpro India and the B.C. Jindal group among global suppliers. Stocks were mixed: Xpro, Cosmo and SRF rose modestly, and Jindal Poly fell about 9% from 24 Oct. Q2 FY27 results from Xpro and Cosmo, with dates not yet announced, are the next real test.
key_points: New this week: QYResearch (7 Aug 2026) puts the global capacitor-grade BOPP film market at USD 874.53 mn in 2025, reaching USD 1,336.23 mn by 2032 (6.25% CAGR). The top three vendors held about 33% of 2025 revenue. Xpro India and the B.C. Jindal group are among the named players (S24).

IndexBox (28 Sep 2026), re-checked this week, forecasts 6-9% annual growth in global dielectric capacitor-film demand over 2026-2035 (7.5% base case), with automotive/EV power electronics fastest at 10-14% a year and a shift to 2-4 micron films (S1).

SRF remains the most aggressive new domestic producer. On its 22 Oct Q2 FY27 call, management said capacitor-grade film has key customer approvals and is selling ahead of plan at 'a significant premium to vanilla film' (S23). A second line is 'likely sooner than later' (S25). We found no board approval for that line as of 29 Oct.

Xpro India is still the only listed company that reports dielectric film separately: FY26 sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S18). Its India capacity doubled to 8,000 MT/yr in Mar 2026, and it targets 13,000 MT by 2027 including a UAE line (S19). Q2 FY27 results were not yet out as of 29 Oct.

Cosmo First's capacitor page, re-checked on 29 Oct, still rates the metalliser at 900 MT/yr and calls the second metalliser a 'forthcoming launch' (S3). The Dec 2023 launch was at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2).

JPFL Films (Jindal Poly) has 5,000 TPA of capacitor capacity operational per CRISIL, which has the ratings on Watch Negative (S8). The Rs 250 cr doubling (S4) is still unconfirmed. The SEBI show-cause notice dated 6 Aug 2026 remains open, with no penalty imposed per the company's filing (S7).

Valuations (Screener, 28 Oct): Xpro trades at 70.8x P/E (S20), Cosmo at 11.5x (S15) and SRF at 30.5x (S17); Jindal Poly is loss-making at 0.96x book (S16). All four are 25-37% below their 52-week highs (S15, S16, S17, S20).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: SRF: capacitor film is commercial ahead of plan at a premium price, and a second line is likely (S23, S25). It is still small next to trailing group sales of Rs 18,265 cr (S17).
Xpro India has the most direct exposure: dielectric film was Rs 135.52 cr of FY26 sales (S18), with capacity heading to 13,000 MT by 2027 (S19). At 70.8x P/E (S20), much of this is already priced in.
Cosmo First's 'series' metallised grade targets drives, renewable inverters, UPS and EVs (S3). At 11.5x P/E and 1.19x book (S15), the stock carries no capacitor premium.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Domestic supply is building quickly. SRF is selling and plans a second line (S25), Xpro is going to 13,000 MT (S19), JPFL runs 5,000 TPA (S8), Cosmo plans a second metalliser (S3), and ECMS has approved several metallised-film projects (S12, S13). No source quantifies Indian demand.
Polypropylene resin is 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). QYResearch's player list is dominated by Chinese producers (S24).
Jindal Poly: an open SEBI notice (S7), ratings on Watch Negative (S8), a trailing net loss of Rs 991 cr and June-quarter sales down 23.9% YoY (S16).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Xpro India's Q2 FY27 results (date not yet announced) for Barjora ramp-up volumes and UAE line progress (S18, S19).
Cosmo First's Q2 FY27 results (date not yet announced) for any capacitor-film or second-metalliser disclosure (S3, S22).
An SRF board decision on a second capacitor-film line, and first capacitor-foil sales in Q3 FY27 (S23, S25).
Finance Ministry notification of DGTR's PET-film anti-dumping recommendation (S9). None found as of 29 Oct, and the case does not cover BOPP.

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film (the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates), mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP). It is vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting at 2.5-12 micron, for AC and DC capacitors (S2). Xpro India makes 2-16 micron base film, including ultra-thin, hazy and semi-rough grades for power capacitors, EV systems and railways (S18). Packaging BOPP is thicker and has no comparable purity or surface requirements. The thin metal layer also lets the capacitor self-heal: a local short burns the metal away instead of destroying the part.

Demand is moving to thinner films that withstand higher voltages. IndexBox says EV demand is shifting to 2-4 micron BOPP, and compact inverter designs push the same way. It expects BOPP to keep 60-70% of volume and metallised film to account for 40-50% of value (S1). Cosmo's metallised grades run from Al-Zn standard (fans, motor-run and AC capacitors), through slope/RMF (APFC panels, wind turbines) and segmented (power supplies, DC-DC converters), to 'series' grades (variable-frequency drives, renewable inverters, UPS, EVs) (S3). Xpro calls demand 'structural, not cyclical', driven by electrification, renewables, grid modernisation and traction (S18).

blocks.title: Global capacitor-grade BOPP film market (QYResearch forecast)

blocks.text: The two forecasts broadly agree on mid-to-high single-digit growth. QYResearch's player list includes Toray, Oji, Shin-Etsu, Bolloré, Tervakoski and several Chinese producers, plus Xpro India and the B.C. Jindal group from India (S24). Mordor and FMI figures were not re-verified and are left out.

When it launched in Dec 2023, Cosmo said capacitor film was largely imported from China and saw room for both import substitution and exports (S2). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). We found no official tonnage series for India's capacitor-film imports.

DGTR has recommended anti-dumping duties of USD 54-366/t on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand (S9). As of 29 Oct we found no Finance Ministry notification. The case covers PET film, not BOPP, the main capacitor dielectric (S1). We found no capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action.

blocks.title: Xpro India dielectric film nameplate capacity
blocks.source: Source: Xpro India FY26 MD&A and FilingReader (S18, S19)

blocks.text: SRF: on the 22 Oct Q2 FY27 call, management said capacitor-grade film is already commercial, with key customer approvals, sales ahead of the original timeline and pricing at 'a significant premium to vanilla film' (S23). It also has key-customer approvals for capacitor aluminium foil, with sales expected from Q3 FY27 (S23). Revenue of the Performance Films & Foil segment rose 51% YoY to Rs 2,122 cr (S25). SRF does not disclose capacitor-film revenue.

Xpro India: FY26 dielectric volume was 3,541 MT versus 3,556 MT in FY25, with net sales of Rs 135.52 cr versus Rs 136.34 cr. Volumes were flat because the new line started only at year-end (S18). FY26 PAT was Rs 30.52 cr (S19). Screener shows June-quarter sales up 20.4% YoY (S20). Q2 FY27, the first full quarter-on-quarter read of the Barjora ramp-up, is still due.

Cosmo First: Q1 FY27 net revenue was Rs 1,166 cr. The company says its capex cycle is complete and deleveraging has begun (S22). It discloses no capacitor-film revenue, and its website still describes the second metalliser as forthcoming (S3).

Jindal Poly Films: CRISIL says JPFL has 5,000 TPA of capacitor capacity operational after the May 2025 Nashik fire, and has the ratings on Watch Negative (S8). Screener shows a trailing net loss of Rs 991 cr and June-quarter sales down 23.9% YoY (S16). The company says the 6 Aug 2026 SEBI notice concerns certain transactions and governance, and that no penalty has been imposed so far (S7).
Only Xpro India reports capacitor-film volume and revenue separately. Any capacitor-film share for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly would be an estimate, so none is given.

items: New this week: Pan Electronics (India), BSE 517397, is a ~Rs 10 cr micro-cap. It has made metallised polypropylene and polyester dielectric films in Bengaluru since 1986 on three metallisation lines, and has moved into MPP capacitors (S14, S21). Its June-quarter sales were about Rs 1 cr (S21), so it is a tiny metalliser and potential base-film buyer, not a scale play.
Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and power-factor panels, so it is a potential domestic film buyer (S5). We found no disclosed film-supply tie-up.

Polyplex and UFlex (Flex Films) are listed by IndexBox among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1), but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade. UFlex's own site lists BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised packaging films (S6). The PET-film anti-dumping case is more relevant to Polyplex (S9).

blocks.text: Coverage gap: the main domestic film-capacitor makers (TDK India, Vishay India) and the ECMS metallisers (Dhruv, Capfilm) are unlisted or not confirmed as listed (S12, S13). The listed exposure is small caps (Xpro, Cosmo, Jindal Poly), one micro-cap metalliser (Pan Electronics) and one large cap where the business is small (SRF). We found no mid-cap pure play. Garware Hi-Tech was dropped this week: its polyester range (10-350 micron) sits above the capacitor band.

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Price-to-book of confirmed capacitor-film producers, 28 Oct 2026

blocks.text: Since 24 Oct, Xpro (+3%), Cosmo (+2%) and SRF (+2%) are up, while Jindal Poly is down about 9% (S15, S16, S17, S20). We found no capacitor-specific news behind these moves. Only Xpro, the one producer with large, disclosed exposure, trades at a theme-style multiple (S20). Cosmo's June-quarter sales rose 45.8% YoY, yet it trades at 11.5x P/E (S15). We could not confirm 6- and 12-month returns from a source we opened, so they are left out.

Broker and media coverage is still thin. ICICI Direct's 24 Jul 2026 SRF note covers capacitor-grade BOPP only as part of SRF's shift to specialty films, and expected near-full utilisation by Q1-Q2 FY28 (S10). SRF's Q2 coverage (S23, S25) is call write-ups that mention capacitor film alongside chemicals and battery foil. We found no Indian broker note built around capacitor film this week.

items: Resin cost: polypropylene is 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1), most of India's imports came from China (S2), and Chinese firms make up much of QYResearch's player list (S24).
Domestic supply build-out: SRF's second line (S25), Xpro to 13,000 MT (S19), JPFL at 5,000 TPA (S8) and Cosmo's second metalliser (S3), against domestic demand no source quantifies.
Small share of revenue: packaging-film cycles dominate earnings at Cosmo, Jindal Poly and SRF (S15, S16, S17).
Governance: Jindal Poly's open SEBI show-cause notice (S7) and CRISIL's Watch Negative (S8).
Q2 FY27 results from Xpro India and Cosmo First (dates not yet announced), for dielectric volumes and the second metalliser (S3, S18, S22).
An SRF board decision on a second capacitor-film line, and first capacitor-foil sales in Q3 FY27 (S23, S25).
Commissioning of Xpro's UAE line and confirmation of JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S4, S8, S19).
ECMS metallised-film projects (Dhruv, Capfilm) coming on stream, and any new ECMS tranche (S12, S13).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S9). No capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action has been found.

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Moving into capacitor-grade BOPP as part of a shift to specialty films (S10). Holds an ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S11), and is selling commercially with key customer approvals (S23).
companies.impact: Sales are ahead of plan at a premium to standard film, and a second line is likely (S23, S25). That is small within Rs 18,265 cr of group sales (S17), but SRF is the fastest-scaling domestic competitor.

companies.name: Xpro India Ltd
companies.role: Dedicated BOPP dielectric base-film maker at Barjora, making 2-16 micron grades. FY26 dielectric sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S18), and India capacity doubled to 8,000 MT in Mar 2026 (S19). QYResearch names it among global players (S24).
companies.impact: The most direct exposure, with a 13,000 MT target by 2027 (S19). It trades at 70.8x P/E (S20) while SRF scales up faster than planned (S23).

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP: launched Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2); the metalliser is now rated 900 MT/yr, with a second forthcoming (S3).
companies.impact: Capacitor film is undisclosed, and earnings follow packaging film (S22). It trades at 11.5x P/E (S15).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film: 5,000 TPA is operational per CRISIL (S8), and a Rs 250 cr doubling was announced in 2024 (S4). QYResearch lists the B.C. Jindal group among global players (S24).
companies.impact: Fire recovery, a Rs 991 cr trailing loss and the open SEBI notice outweigh the capacitor theme (S7, S8, S16).

companies.name: Pan Electronics (India) Ltd
companies.role: Micro-cap Bengaluru metalliser of polypropylene and polyester dielectric films since 1986, now also making MPP capacitors (S14, S21).
companies.impact: A potential buyer of domestic base film, but at ~Rs 10 cr market cap and ~Rs 1 cr of quarterly sales, the exposure is immaterial in investment terms (S21).

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S5).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer as local supply grows; no film-supply tie-up has been disclosed (S5).

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker that IndexBox lists among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade. The PET-film anti-dumping case is more relevant to it (S9).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Its Flex Films business makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised films (S6); IndexBox lists it among Indian producers (S1).
companies.impact: Has metallising know-how, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S6).

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W43 edition, researched on 29 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. Re-opened this week: IndexBox (figures unchanged), Cosmo's capacitor-film page (still 900 MT/yr, second metalliser forthcoming) and BigMint on the PET-film anti-dumping case. Searches found no Q2 FY27 results or board-meeting notice yet for Xpro India or Cosmo First, no new ECMS tranche, no Finance Ministry duty notification, no SRF board approval for a second capacitor line, no update on the Jindal Poly SEBI matter and no JPFL doubling confirmation. Added this week: the QYResearch market sizing, and Pan Electronics (micro-cap metalliser, found while checking for listed downstream capacitor makers). Cited from a third-party profile, not company filings. Garware Hi-Tech and the Polyplex product page were dropped to keep sources at 25. Polyplex and UFlex stay as 'other' because only IndexBox names them, with no company confirmation. Valuations are the Screener figures supplied with this edition (28 Oct 2026); 24 Oct prices are from last week's edition. Source IDs were renumbered. Some company-website dates are access dates. Not stated because not confirmed: capacitor-film revenue for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly, Indian import tonnage, and 6/12-month stock returns. No ratings or price targets are given.
